look_here_first: Find one PETIOLE with its small paired CUP-LIKE NECTAR GLANDS near blade, then inspect MULTIPLE leaves on the same vine: often narrow fingerlike/birdwing primary lobes with secondary lobes; size and lobing vary widely. Compare glandless P. lutea and its broad rounded lobes. Small greenish flowers have five sepals (6–10 mm long) but no petals; ripening small dark berries support.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: perennial prostrate or low-climbing vine with slender coiling tendrils

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: petiole glandular with paired saucer- or cup-shaped glands near the blade

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaf blades extremely variable but deeply 3–9-lobed

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: primary lobes narrow and acute; lateral lobes often long and spreading

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: primary lobes may themselves be lobed, creating a birdwing/handlike silhouette

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: petals absent; five green sepals (each 6–10 mm long) and two whorls of corona filaments form the showy portion

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: ripe berries small, globose, dark blue to black

lookalikes.differences: Passiflora lutea: P. lutea has glandless petioles and broad rounded 3-lobed leaves; P. tenuiloba has paired cuplike petiole glands and narrow deeply dissected lobes. Passiflora incarnata: Both have petiole glands, but P. incarnata has much broader serrated 3-lobed leaves, huge purple/white flowers and large green-yellow maypops. P. tenuiloba has narrow entire lobes and tiny petal-less green flowers. Passiflora affinis: Another small green-flowered Central/West Texas passionflower. Use leaf architecture and gland characters; P. tenuiloba typically has the distinctive narrow deeply divided birdwing leaves. Important: FNA says FIVE sepals, each 6–10 mm long; do not interpret the measurement as a sepal count.
